analysis.title: BXP Inc. (BXP): 3Q26 First Take: Another beat-and-raise quarter; 2nd generation net rent spreads up HSD
key_insights: BXP reported 3Q26 FFOPS of $1.89, +5.2% vs GS estimate of $1.80, +4.7% vs FactSet consensus of $1.81, and +8.6% y/y. The beat vs GS was driven by lower property operating expenses and a higher JV contribution (including lease termination fees), partly offset by higher interest expense and G&A.
BXP had guided to $1.80-$1.82 for 3Q26 FFO and attributed the beat to better-than-projected portfolio performance.

FY26 FFOPS guidance was raised at the low end by 7 cents and the high end by 3 cents to $7.06-$7.08. The midpoint rose to $7.07 from $7.02 (+70bps, +0.4% vs GS estimate), implying FY FFOPS growth of +2.97%. The FY raise was smaller than the 3Q beat, and GS will look for an explanation on the call.
FY26 GAAP same-store NOI growth guidance was raised at the low end by 55bps and the high end by 15bps to 2.35%-2.75%, with the midpoint up 35bps to 2.55% from 2.20%.

GS expects BXP could slightly outperform the REIT sector on Wednesday 10/28/2026, citing occupancy gains, leasing spreads (net rent on 2nd generation leases +9.33%), the guidance raise and the 3Q FFOPS beat vs consensus. Limiting factors are the smaller FY raise than the 3Q beat and slower leasing volume in 3Q.
3Q26 same-store NOI growth excluding termination income was +3.4% GAAP and -0.3% cash, vs +3.5% and +0.8% in 2Q26.

In-service occupancy was 89.4%, up 100bps q/q and +340bps y/y. The leased rate is 91.9%, so the signed-not-occupied spread is 250bps. About 50% of the 1.1mn sqft of SNO space is expected to commence in 2026. Same-property occupancy rose 230bps y/y to 89.5%, and suburban San Francisco was the only sub-market that declined.
Lease volume commenced in 3Q26 was just over 1.5mn sqft, +31% y/y for the quarter and +80.5% y/y on a TTM basis. 2nd generation space commenced was up 46% for the quarter.
Leases executed in 3Q26 were just over 1.2mn sqft, down 20.7% y/y and down 2.7% y/y on a TTM basis. GS wants management's view on continued leasing of vacant space and the status of early renewals.

Gross/net rent spreads on 3Q26 executed 2nd generation leases (1.12mn sqft) were +6.55%/+9.33%. Spreads were negative in San Francisco and Boston, positive in New York, Seattle and Washington DC, and flat in Los Angeles. Weighted average free rent period, transaction cost PSF and lease cost per year of term all rose sequentially.

343 Madison: BXP closed a $1.2bn construction loan (four-year initial term, one-year extension, Term SOFR +250 declining to +225 on milestones) and sold a 10.55% equity interest to AVRS Partners, which committed $81.5mn ($50.7mn funded at closing). BXP keeps 89.45% and control. The 930k sqft project is 56% pre-leased, including the 148k sqft McDermott Will & Schulte lease. Initial occupancy is scheduled for 3Q29 and stabilization for 2Q31.

Reservoir Place (363k sqft) is 89% leased, mainly through the 322k sqft Boston Dynamics lease. Initial occupancy and stabilization are expected in 2Q27. BXP's estimated investment is $87mn with $72mn of future equity required.

Worldgate Drive multifamily in Herndon, VA (359 units, BXP owns 20%) has initial occupancy expected in 3Q28 and stabilization in 2Q30, with expected total investment of $26.4mn. 290 Binney Street was placed in service in 2Q26 and is 100% leased, with BXP's share of investment at $488mn excluding electrical-vault work.

During 3Q26 BXP sold Sumner Square and 1330 Connecticut Avenue in Washington DC for an aggregate $155.4mn gross, with $150.3mn net proceeds and about $10.5mn of book gains. It acquired 860 and 870 Winter Street in Waltham, MA for $30.3mn.

Year-to-date dispositions are $681.0mn gross and $519.5mn net cash proceeds ($569.7mn including the 343 Madison equity sale). Since the September 2025 Investor Day, gross asset sales are about $1.62bn, or 85.3% of the $1,900mn target, leaving $278.7mn. GS models $148.7mn of dispositions in 4Q26 and $158mn in 2027.

Call topics for GS: drivers of better-than-projected portfolio performance, SF and DC leasing outlook, balance sheet priorities after the $700mn bond issuance and upcoming debt maturities, and whether BXP still expects to meet its Investor Day disposition target.
GS rates BXP Neutral with a 12-month price target of $70, based on a Q5-Q8 target AFFO multiple of 17.1x. The stock closed at $60.89 on 27 Oct 2026, implying 15.0% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $70 target (17.1x Q5-Q8 AFFO) after a 3Q26 FFOPS beat and FY guidance raise. It expects slight REIT sector outperformance on 10/28 but flags a smaller FY raise than the 3Q beat and slower leasing volume.

sector_views.rationale: BXP occupancy is approaching 90% with a geographically diversified portfolio, ahead of NYC-focused VNO and SLG per GS Exhibit 1. Leasing spreads were up high-single-digits in net rent terms but negative in San Francisco and Boston.

earnings_insights: BXP 3Q26 FFOPS reported $1.89 vs GS estimate $1.80 and FactSet consensus $1.81, +8.6% y/y. Company guidance for 3Q26 was $1.80-$1.82.
FY26 FFOPS guidance raised to $7.06-$7.08 (midpoint $7.07 vs prior $7.02), implying +2.97% FY growth. GS FY26E FFOPS is $7.05.
FY26 GAAP same-store NOI growth guidance raised to 2.35%-2.75% (midpoint 2.55% vs prior 2.20%).
3Q26 same-store NOI growth excluding termination income was +3.4% GAAP and -0.3% cash, vs +3.5% and +0.8% in 2Q26.
GS FFOPS estimates: 12/26E $7.05, 12/27E $7.17, 12/28E $7.52; quarterly 9/26E $1.80 (the estimate the 3Q26 print of $1.89 was measured against), 12/26E $1.89, 3/27E $1.70.
risk_factors: Higher or lower leasing spreads or occupancy.
Higher or lower development or acquisition contributions to NOI.
Lower or higher interest rates, which affect interest expense.
FY guidance raise smaller than the 3Q beat and slower 3Q leasing volume could limit outperformance.
Executed lease volume fell 20.7% y/y in 3Q26.
Negative leasing spreads in San Francisco and Boston, and suburban San Francisco occupancy decline.

tension_points.bull_case: Net rent on 2nd generation leases rose 9.33%, occupancy gained 100bps q/q to 89.4%, and commenced lease volume rose 31% y/y with a 91.9% leased rate leaving 250bps of signed-not-occupied space to come.
tension_points.bear_case: Executed lease volume fell 20.7% y/y in 3Q26, the FY guidance raise was smaller than the 3Q beat, and spreads were negative in San Francisco and Boston.

theme_stances.key_argument: Occupancy gains, high-single-digit net rent spreads and a raised FY guide support slight REIT sector outperformance for BXP.
theme_stances.evidence: we believe BXP could outperform the REIT sector slightly
